_comment: THIS REPO'S OWN SETTINGS. Adapted from core/.claude/settings.template.json,
which is payload -- a seed for the NEXT consumer, not this repo's configuration.
Editing the template does not change anything here, and editing this file does
not change what a consumer is seeded with.
Adapted from the template as its own notes instruct:
env.DATABASE_URL      dropped -- there is no database here.
hooks.SessionStart    dropped -- it points at scripts/setup-test-db.sh,
which this repo does not have.
permissions.deny      the drizzle-kit entries are dropped (no Drizzle here);
Read(**/.env*) is kept, because it applies everywhere.
model                 kept as opus: this repo is almost entirely payload code.
THE HOOK PATH IS ABSOLUTE, VIA ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, AND BOTH HALVES MATTER.
Absolute, because a hook command is resolved against the CURRENT WORKING
DIRECTORY, not the project root -- Claude Code's hooks reference says so and
says to prefer path placeholders. The earlier relative form
`bash core/.claude/guard.sh` worked only while the cwd happened to be the repo
root: from core/ it resolved core/core/.claude/guard.sh and bash exited 127,
and PreToolUse treats every non-zero exit OTHER than 2 as non-blocking. So one
`cd core` silently disarmed the merge gate, the review-round budget and the
destructive-command guard at once. Measured: exit 127 then, exit 2 now, from
core/scripts and from /tmp alike. (Codex, PR #10 round 4, P1.)
...and it points at the PAYLOAD, `core/.claude/guard.sh`, rather than a symlink
at `.claude/guard.sh`, because guard.sh locates its decision script as
`dirname($BASH_SOURCE)/../scripts/guard-decision.mjs`, and $BASH_SOURCE is the
path AS INVOKED, not the resolved target. Through a symlink that resolves to
<repo>/scripts/guard-decision.mjs, which does not exist here -- node would exit
1, and by the same non-blocking rule the tool call would PROCEED.
Both failure modes are the same shape and it is the one that matters here: a
guard that cannot launch does not refuse, it waves the call through. A broken
guard that fails open is worse than no guard.
A THIRD INSTANCE OF THAT SHAPE, now closed (issue #11): guard-decision.mjs
decided whether it was invoked directly by comparing import.meta.url against a
hand-built `file://` string. Those differ whenever the checkout path needs
escaping -- a space, a `#` -- and the script then exited 0 having evaluated
nothing, which guard.sh reads as ALLOW. It now compares
pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href, which encodes the same way import.meta.url
does, and a static check in each test suite refuses the old form.
WHAT IS STILL OPEN is the shape itself, tracked as issue #16: guard.sh reads
ANY non-2 exit as allow, so the next failure to produce a verdict fails open by
the same logic. Closing it means changing this hook protocol -- a sentinel on
the allow path, so a run that allowed is distinguishable from one that never
happened.
The three PreToolUse entries are not optional. They are the local half of the
branch-protection story; the other half is the ruleset on main, which is in
place (main is protected). Keep the longer timeout on the merge matcher -- the
merge guard reads live GitHub state and 5s is not enough for it.
